newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Horta says Gusmao should have got Peace Prize.
newsitem.headline: Horta says Gusmao should have got Peace Prize.

text.p: Jose Ramos Horta, the exiled East Timorese resistance leader who on Friday was named joint winner of the Nobel Peace Prize, said it should have gone not to him but to the jailed resistance head Xanana Gusmao.
Ramos Horta, who has led the international campaign against Indonesian rule in the former Portuguese colony, told Reuters: "I would feel much happier if, instead of my name, his was selected."
Indonesia invaded East Timor in 1975 after the abrupt departure of its Portuguese colonisers. It annexed the territory the following year in a move never recognised by the United Nations.
Ramos Horta, who spends much of his time in Sydney, was on Friday named joint winner of the 1996 Peace Prize with Bishop Carlos Belo, East Timor's outspoken Catholic bishop.

"I'm happy but surprised, because Bishop Belo deserves the Nobel Peace Prize, but the other person who should be sharing the award with him is my leader, Xanana Gusmao," he told Reuters by telephone from his mother's home in Sydney.
"He's an outstanding man of peace and democracy, a man of courage," he said, adding that he hoped the prize would send a signal to Jakarta "that the people of East Timor have suffered long enough".
